links.comparator_used: Randomized rollout to half of patients; the other half presumably had standard human-support handling of queries without the risk-stratified assistant (comparator arm not described in detail in the abstract)
links.outcome: Human support workload, human response time, clinical safety and resolution of inquiries
links.effect: 65% fewer standard-risk queries routed to human support; average human response time 9.6 to 3.6 minutes; 96% accurate guidance, 0% critical safety events, no AI-generated diagnoses; improved resolution without additional visits
links.quote: Using a randomized rollout to half of the patient population, the authors found that the risk-stratified assistant maintained a high level of clinical safety (96% accurate guidance, 0% critical safety events, and no AI-generated diagnoses) while reducing standard-risk queries routed to human support by 65%, shortening average human response times from 9.6 to 3.6 minutes, and improving resolution of health inquiries without additional visits.

design_hint: risk stratification guardrails with escalation pathways and human-in-the-loop auditing
